← Developer · Student guide
← How matching works

More useful matches. Fewer assumptions.

54 fictional student stories across all 12 fields. Each combines the official interest assessment, daily-work preferences and focused follow-ups.

What changed

  • Zero to three supported pathways. No filler cards.
  • Daily-work conflicts stay visible and keep a field out of recommendations.
  • Clinical follow-ups compare physician, NP, PA, RN, dentist, hygienist and assistant work.
  • Repeated, focused task interests can put a career in the main suggestions even with partial RIASEC overlap. Scores and labels stay unchanged.

These are software and guidance reviews, not observations of real students. The 54 stories contain 38 distinct six-score patterns. Some intentionally share the same interests to test how different follow-up choices refine them. There is no measured predictive accuracy.

R hands-on · I investigation · A creative · S helping · E persuasion · C organization. Scores: 0–40.
